p:ISR: Israel's money is the shekel and its central bank is the Bank of Israel. It scores 26 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and no government pressure was reported between 2010 and 2018. Ministerial pressure came later. Through 2025 finance minister Bezalel Smotrich publicly pressed governor Amir Yaron to cut interest rates, calling the decision to hold the rate at 4 percent wrong and asking him to reverse it, and on 4 September 2025 telling business leaders that if the governor would not lower rates he would lower taxes instead. The bank answered that the governor and the Monetary Committee decide on professional grounds alone; Smotrich said in the same remarks that the bank's independence was critical and that he had no intention of interfering. On 29 April 2002 State Comptroller Eliezer Goldberg reported that former governor Jacob Frenkel unlawfully received hundreds of thousands of shekels when he resigned, approved by a senior official who reported to him; Goldberg did not say whether the money should be demanded back. On 3 February 2009 Globes reported that a draft comptroller report alleged flaws in the bank's supervision of Bank Hapoalim's sub-prime investments, on which Hapoalim wrote off 1.5 billion dollars; the bank said it had responses to all the points, and this is unproven. A comptroller report on 17 October 2012 found supervision of the bank's reserves dealing deficient as those reserves grew from 28 to 75 billion dollars; the bank said some issues had been corrected during the audit. Frenkel, governor from 1991 to 2000, came from the International Monetary Fund and later chaired Merrill Lynch International; he sits in the Group of Thirty alongside private-sector members such as Jane Fraser of Citi and Philipp Hildebrand of BlackRock. Stanley Fischer, governor from 2005 to 2013, came from the World Bank, the IMF and Citigroup. The bank is also one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements.
p:CZE: The Czech National Bank issues the koruna and scores 20 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, leaving it less exposed than 95 percent of the places measured. It is one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements, the bank used by central banks themselves. Ales Michl was an economist and investment strategist at Raiffeisenbank from 2006 to 2015 and an external economic adviser to the finance ministry from 2014 to 2018 and later to Prime Minister Andrej Babis, joined the bank's board in December 2018 and was then appointed governor in succession to Jiri Rusnok. Czech Television reports that he founded Michl Fund Management in 2016, which co-founded the qualified-investor fund Robot Asset Management SICAV, that he later placed the company in a trust, and that some experts believe he may still have influence over it, which he denies; no ethics finding is recorded. In 2026 police arrested a long-serving employee accused of misappropriating tens of millions of koruna, after suspicious transactions on his account were flagged; the bank confirmed the theft was being investigated at its Brno branch, and the accusation is unproven. Government pressure was reported in 3 of the 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018, all of it pressing for tighter policy, alongside three threats to replace leaders. The president of the Czech Republic appoints all seven members of the bank board alone, and on 18 February 2015 President Milos Zeman said he would appoint nobody who favoured devaluing the koruna and would name members who backed adopting the euro, at a time when the bank was holding the koruna weak against the euro; Andrej Babis, then finance minister, called that an unacceptable interference with the bank's independence. Zeman had five of the seven seats to fill before March 2018, and the bank kept the policy. State Street Global Advisors has held an equity mandate from the bank since 2007, since raised to 7.5 billion US dollars, and also advises it on alternatives to its reserve strategies; BNP Paribas Asset Management agreed a 500 million dollar mortgage-backed securities mandate in November 2019; and Ernst & Young Audit, s.r.o. audits the accounts. Some of the gold is kept in the bank's own high-security vault in Prague, mostly for making its gold coins, with most of the reserve stored in London under no named institution, which is storage rather than management. A commemorative banknote marking the establishment of the Czechoslovak currency, which entered circulation on 30 March 2022, carries the imprint of Statni tiskarna cenin; who prints the circulating notes is not stated.
p:SVK: Slovakia uses the euro, so the National Bank of Slovakia does not set interest rates; the European Central Bank does that for the 21 euro countries. The Slovak bank is also one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements, whose capital is held by central banks alone. Slovakia's own case ended in a conviction: on 29 May 2025 the Specialised Criminal Court found the sitting governor, Kazimir, guilty of paying a 48,000 euro bribe in 2017 and 2018, while he was finance minister, to the head of the tax office in connection with audits of private companies, and fined him 200,000 euros. He denied wrongdoing and said he would appeal, and the offence predates his central bank post. Two findings concern the European Central Bank. The European Ombudsman found maladministration over president Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a private forum of central bankers and bank executives, and recommended in January 2018 that he suspend it; the ECB declined and he did not. And Coeure's remark to a private London event on 18 May 2015 that the ECB would front-load asset purchases was published only the next morning, which the ECB put down to an internal procedure error. The Slovak bank owns 31.694 tonnes of gold in bars, stored for it by the Bank of England as depositary, which safekeeps rather than manages it. Deloitte Audit s.r.o. audited its accounts and Grant Thornton Audit, s.r.o. is the approved auditor for 2024 to 2027. Governor Jozef Makuch told the bank's Banking Council on 27 November 2018 that he would leave in March 2019, two years before his term ended, so that his successor would be chosen before the 2020 general election rather than by the parliament that followed it; he argued that appointing a governor early would strengthen the bank's independence, and no source reports anyone pressing him to go. He stayed until Kazimir was appointed on 1 June 2019. Slovakia scores 25 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.
p:PRT: Portugal uses the euro, so interest rates are set by the European Central Bank for all 21 European Union countries on the currency rather than by the Banco de Portugal, which has its notes printed by Valora S.A., a printer it owns. It scores 28 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. Governor Carlos Costa says prime minister Antonio Costa telephoned him on 12 April 2016, while the bank was stripping Isabel dos Santos of her fitness to sit on the board of EuroBic, and said the daughter of the president of a country friendly to Portugal could not be treated badly. The two sides agree the call happened and disagree what it was: Observador reported a written message in which the prime minister confirmed the call and said he had considered the removal inopportune, while the prime minister told parliament he had never made any approach in her favour, called the account false and filed a civil action, which the former governor answered with one of his own; both were dropped by agreement in May 2025. The bank did not change the decision and Isabel dos Santos was removed from the board. A 600-page report by a committee the bank itself appointed, with technical support from Boston Consulting Group, pointed to failures in its supervision of Banco Espirito Santo going back to the start of the previous decade, and said information on the Espirito Santo group and on the bank's operations in Angola was reportedly not used; the Banco de Portugal twice refused parliament's request for the report. On 20 July 2021 Fernando Anastacio, rapporteur of parliament's inquiry into losses at Novo Banco, presented a draft report saying supervision had failed across the board, which remained a draft that the PSD said its deputies would vote against. The committee approved its final report on 27 July 2021, concluding that the rescue of Banco Espirito Santo and the first capitalisation of Novo Banco, of 4,900 million euros, were a political fraud, with criticism of the Banco de Portugal and the European Commission and no officials named. In April 2019, after an EY audit of the management of Caixa Geral de Depositos, the bank's ethics committee examined governor Carlos Costa's request to be excused from matters concerning that bank, where he had been a board member from 2004 to 2006; no conclusion was published. Two findings concern the European Central Bank itself: the European Ombudsman found maladministration over President Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum that includes private financiers, and recommended in January 2018 that he suspend it, which the bank declined; and a speech by Coeure to a private London event on 18 May 2015, saying asset purchases would be front-loaded, was published only the next morning, which the ECB put down to an internal procedure error. Vitor Constancio was governor from 1985 to 1986, an executive director of Banco Portugues de Investimento from 1995 to 2000, governor again until May 2010 and then ECB Vice-President, with no ethics finding recorded. PricewaterhouseCoopers & Associados audits the accounts for 2022 to 2026. Of 382.7 tonnes of gold, about 45 per cent was kept in the bank's own vaults in 2023, 49 per cent at the Bank of England, 5 per cent at the Bank for International Settlements and 1 per cent at the Banque de France; those institutions store the metal, they do not manage it.
